chapter_title: Concerning the Catechumen who found fault with the

fills.notes: The quarrel is explained immediately by the presence of the “old man” dwelling in their body. In the oldest substrate the causal link is structural: contention arises *in/through the body* as the mixed vessel where contrary essences press against one another. Thus a short locative phrase that anticipates “because the old man too dwells in their body” fits the correspondential logic.

The sequence demands: offence → hardening/striking → dispute. In the substrate register, ‘taking offence’ is not moralizing but the reaction of the mixed state: the evil in the body seizes on what is infirm in the other’s outer person. A phrase like “at each other’s weakness,” coheres with the earlier theme (hard words to faces; foreign body; Flesh of Sin) and leads naturally into “they dispute with one another.”

assessment: Two lacunae are trivial (letter/word) and are certain. The two gaps in ¶11 are restorably constrained by the causal structure (quarrel arises in the bodily vessel because the old man is present; offence leads into mutual dispute), but the exact Coptic translator’s wording cannot be recovered with certainty.
